old: `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` starts work eagerly on the current thread until the first suspension.
new: `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` eagerly enters top-level `launch` / `async` children of `runTest`, which helps install collectors before emitting. It does not guarantee a universal execution order for nested or subsequently queued work.
reason: Qualify eager-entry guarantee and avoid treating Unconfined scheduling as production ordering.

old: `backgroundScope` is cancelled automatically when `runTest` finishes, which prevents never-ending hot-flow collectors from hanging the test.
new: `backgroundScope` is cancelled when `runTest` finishes. Use `runCurrent()` to run its currently queued work or `advanceTimeBy()` for timed work: `advanceUntilIdle()` stops advancing once only background-scope tasks remain. Keep finite assertions in the main test scope.
reason: advanceUntilIdle does not drain background work once no foreground tasks remain.

new:
repository.emit(User("Asha"))
    runCurrent() // Process work queued for the background collector now.

    assertEquals(UiState.Content("Asha"), states.last())
reason: Manual hot-flow example must execute background collector before asserting.
Original emits before queued collector subscribes, lacks a Flow element type, and relies on advanceUntilIdle for background-only work.

old: This hangs because `StateFlow` never completes. Use Turbine, `first`, `take`, or `backgroundScope`.
new: This collection never completes normally because `StateFlow` is hot. Inside `runTest`, uncompleted foreground work eventually fails at the test timeout; it does not wait forever by default. Use a bounded assertion (`first`, `take`, Turbine) or a collector in `backgroundScope`.
reason: Distinguish never-completing flow contract from runTest timeout.

old: `delay(1.minutes)` does not sleep for one real minute. The scheduler advances instantly when the test tells it to.
new: `delay(1.minutes)` on a test dispatcher uses virtual time. The scheduler can advance explicitly through the time-control APIs or automatically when the test suspends waiting for scheduled work. Delays on real IO/Default dispatchers are not skipped.
reason: runTest also automatically advances virtual time; real-dispatcher delay is outside scheduler.

old: If the rule's dispatcher and `runTest` use different schedulers, pass the scheduler explicitly when creating dependencies:
new: When Main is replaced by a test dispatcher before `runTest` starts, the test normally adopts that scheduler. Keep all dependencies on it. A new dispatcher constructed with a different scheduler is not repaired merely by advancing the test scheduler; reconstruct it using the shared scheduler:
reason: Clarify Main scheduler adoption and avoid implying independent dispatchers are advanced together.

old: - A state: active, suspended, cancelling, cancelled, or completed.
new: - A Job lifecycle state such as active, cancelling, cancelled, or completed. Suspension is an execution condition: a suspended coroutine can still have an active Job.
reason: Suspended is not a separate Job lifecycle state.

old: If cancellation is swallowed, parent scopes believe work completed normally while child work may have skipped cleanup or hidden an aborted operation.
new: Swallowing a cancellation exception does not reactivate a Job that was cancelled by its owner. It can still let later ordinary statements execute or turn an operation-local cancellation into an apparent success value. `finally` still runs; preserve cancellation so callers can observe the intended outcome.
reason: A caught exception cannot reset Job cancellation, and finally cleanup is not skipped by catch.

old: The JVM debug agent can also enrich thread names with coroutine ids and names:
new: The JVM coroutine debug mode can enrich thread names with coroutine ids/names; enable it with this system property (separate from installing DebugProbes instrumentation):
reason: Thread-name debug property is distinct from the dynamic debug-probe agent.

old: This is most useful in local JVM tests and debug builds.
new: For example, `main @coroutine#2` means thread `main`, coroutine number 2; another id on `main` is not another OS thread. This is most useful in local JVM tests and debug builds.
reason: Prevents the observed Playground debug ids from teaching multiple-thread execution.

old: If cleanup must run after cancellation, use `NonCancellable` sparingly and keep it bounded.
new: If cleanup must suspend after owner cancellation, use `NonCancellable` sparingly with a bounded, cooperatively cancellable cleanup operation. A timeout is not a hard interrupt for an arbitrary blocking call, and a cleanup failure can replace an exception already propagating; decide how required cleanup failures are reported.
reason: Clarify cooperative deadline and exception masking around bounded cleanup.
